newsitem.title: UK: Charles gives Camilla 100,000 pound bracelet-paper.
newsitem.headline: Charles gives Camilla 100,000 pound bracelet-paper.

text.p: Prince Charles has given his mistress Camilla Parker Bowles a 100,000 pound ($170,000) diamond bracelet as a token of his love on her 50th birthday, a leading tabloid reported on Sunday.
"This is telling Camilla and the world that she's the most important person in his life," one of the heir to the throne's closest friends told the News of the World.
But Princess Diana, divorced from Charles after much acrimony, was said not to "think or care" about Parker Bowles, according to the controversial tycoon hosting her at his French holiday home.

Britain's royalty-obsessed tabloids on Sunday were packed with details of the most publicly scrutinised private party of the year, where a radiant Parker Bowles was said to have danced cheek to cheek with her lover.

Charles, fearing public opinion was ranged against him after his divorce from Princess Diana, has always been careful never to be photographed together with the woman his wife once angrily called "The Rottweiler".

But the blanket media coverage of her birthday bash at Charles' country home was seen as a way of gradually convincing Britons that Camilla was now a permanent part of Charles' life -- whether he marries again or not.
"A 100,000 pound present from the prince is hugely significant -- he's as cautious a man with money you'll ever meet," his close friend told the News of The World.
One opinion poll last week showed that 68 percent of Britons were now in favour of Charles marrying Camilla.
Diana was the target of criticism for deciding to take her sons, Princes Williams and Harry, to holiday at the French home of controversial tycoon Mohamed Al Fayed.
His sleaze allegations against Conservative ministers were seen to be instrumental in the opposition Labour Party's landslide election victory in May.
Al Fayed, interviewed by the Mail on Sunday, likened Camilla Parker Bowles to "something out of a Dracula film".

He dismissed suggestions that Diana was planning to leave Britain. "She would never leave her kids. She is popular and loved by the people, how could she ever think of going to live abroad?" he asked.

"As for Camilla, Diana doesn't think or care about her from what I can make out. Camilla's like something from a Dracula film compared with the vividly beautiful Diana who is full of life," the Harrods store boss said.
Asked if Diana sporting before paparazzi in a leopardskin swimswuit was a ploy to knock Camilla off the front pages, Al Fayed chortled and said: "Certainly not."
Every curve and bulge in those now notorious photographs was perused by tabloid experts with Doctor Mark Porter telling the Sunday Mirror: "I looked at those pictures and thought -- She's pregnant."

"It is well known that she desperately wants a little girl now she is 36 and running out of time," said the tabloid in a two-page spread about the biological clock said to be ticking away for the world's most photographed woman.
